media_work.title: Chasing Me to My Grave: An Artist's Memoir of the Jim Crow South
media_work.creator_name: Winfred Rembert with Erin I. Kelly
media_work.format: Hardcover, paperback, ebook, 304 pages with 4-color images throughout
media_work.focus_or_theme: Memoir of survival and artistry during the Jim Crow era, including wrongful arrest and incarceration

key_quotes_raw: "Vivid, confrontational, revelatory, and complex, Chasing Me to My Grave is a searing memoir in prose and painted leather that celebrates Black life and summons readers to confront painful and urgent realities at the heart of American society."
"He was arrested and incarcerated in the local jail for more than a year, without charges being filed against him."
systemic_issues_raw: Arbitrary arrest and detention without charges
Racial discrimination in the criminal justice system
Lack of due process for Black Americans in the Jim Crow South
Systemic racism embedded in legal institutions
policy_recommendations_raw: Need for stronger protections against arbitrary detention
Reforms to ensure due process for all defendants
Addressing systemic racism in the criminal justice system
Recognition and redress for historical injustices
additional_resources_raw: Rembert's artwork depicting his experiences in the Jim Crow South
Rembert's survival of a near-fatal lynching attempt
His experiences in Georgia's prison system
His development as an artist who documented his experiences through leather tooling

research_notes_other.this_book_is_particularly_valuable_for_o:
1. Provides a first-person account of wrongful incarceration during the Jim Crow era
2. Illustrates how racial discrimination led to arbitrary detention without formal charges
3. Documents survival through an unjust criminal justice system
4. Shows the intersection of art and memoir as a means of processing trauma from wrongful incarceration
5. Highlights historical patterns of injustice that continue to influence the modern criminal justice system
The book stands out from others in our research as it combines memoir with visual art (Rembert's leather tooling artwork) to tell the story of wrongful incarceration. It also provides historical context for understanding contemporary issues of wrongful conviction by examining the Jim Crow era's legal system. The Pulitzer Prize recognition underscores the significance and quality of this work in documenting this important aspect of American history.

media_item.item_title: Book Content: Chasing Me to My Grave: An Artist's Memoir of the Jim Crow South
media_item.focus_or_theme: Memoir of survival and artistry during the Jim Crow era, including wrongful arrest and incarceration
media_item.summary_notes: A memoir combining prose and painted leather, this book recounts the author's survival and artistic journey during the Jim Crow era.  It details his wrongful arrest and incarceration, highlighting systemic racism and lack of due process within the legal system. The book offers a first-person account of enduring an unjust system,  combining personal narrative with visual art to process trauma and historical injustice.
media_item.case_details_raw: Winfred Rembert, the author, was arrested and incarcerated in Georgia during the 1960s for over a year without formal charges. His imprisonment stemmed from racial discrimination, lack of due process, police misconduct, and systemic racism prevalent in the Jim Crow South. He was eventually released but never formally exonerated.
